These past two years have been difficult. I've been screwed out of money by three people: one was a close family member, one was a friend since childhood, and the other was just a friend. This, combined with the fact that I am having a very difficult time finding a job has been taking it's toll on me both emotionally, physically, and financially.

I know what I'm about to say is going to sound selfish. For that, whoever is reading this (or not) has my apologies.

I have gone out of my way to help people. My first real career was in a field that involved helping troubled teens through their problems. And I mean helped. Blaming all their problems on society was neither encouraged nor allowed. But, I didn't show them the "tough love" of abandonning them to the system, either. I taught them practical skills that they could use to deal with their problems; skills that helped me when I was their age going through my own difficulties. I left the field because one of the teens I was working with died. Long story short, I was so enveloped in making sure those who knew her well were getting by alright that I forgot to deal with how I was impacted by the event. The result was not healthy. It led me to a very cynical place, devoid of any positive emotion; self-imposed isolation followed suit.

Fast forward a few years , and I opened myself up to try and help people again.

The first person I tried to help, a close family member, begged for me to come back to my home city to help them. I discovered some time later that this person had threatened to kill me over the span of several years. The threats were made about me but to other family members. My family is a little old-school when it comes to dealing with family problems, and none of them were really equipped to deal with the threats that were made toward my life. I don't blame them for not knowing what to do; they were in an impossible position. I do not envy the fear or the sense of helplessness my other family member kept them in. Besides, I'm alive, so it worked out- well, except for the $4000 I was screwed out of.

The second person I helped, a childhood friend, was homeless. I gave him and his baby-momma room to live in a large studio apartment I had back in 2013. I ended up cosigning with them for another apartment in 2014. It wasn't entirely altruistic; I needed to move anyways, and I thought I could kill two birds with one stone (help my friend out, and also help ease my financial obligations by splitting the rent). Fast-forward a year, and it turns out that his baby-momma had Borderline Personality Disorder, and he spent all the money he earned (and also some that I loaned him) on impressing other girls and god knows what else. Oh, and he never did pay his half of the rent. In all, I spent about $1820 covering his half of the rent for about 6 months.

The third person was just a friend who I thought had cleaned up his act. He was arrested earlier this week just after finally landing a job. I entered his room, and... well, lets just say that 1) I know where the smell and the flies were coming from, 2) I decided to clean it up for him; I'm on my third garbage bag and I've barely got a quarter of his 100ft (if that) bedroom clean, 3) I now know what a needle disposal case looks like, 4) I have no idea how the fuck I'm going to clean the walls. I don't even know what the fuck that shit is on them, or how he managed to get it on there.

I don't blame them. If anything, I (rightly) blame myself. I am a bad judge of character. A horrible judge of character. I know this is my fault, and every time I try to fix it, I make things worse.

So, this is where I am. Trying to figure how the fuck I'm going to pay my rent. Trying to figure how the fuck I got myself into this position. Trying to figure out if I should, who I should, and when I should ask for help. I know I should ask for help... but I can't. Asking for help, it's not a pride thing. It's... I'm old enough to have my shit together. I should have my shit together. It's not someone else's responsibility to take care of me, or look after me.

The last thing I want to do is put the people I care about in a position where they feel obligated to help me. Someone helped me once before (really, someones, but I count them as a single unit since they're married and very much behave as if they were a single unit). They were a godsend. And I undid every ounce of help they gave me when I decided to move back to this fucking city, this place where everything bad in my life seems to occur.

I don't know what I've done to deserve any of this, but I must have really screwed someone over pretty bad to have this much bad karma. I've applied for a half dozen jobs this week, so maybe something will pan out. Hopefully, something will pan out.

Well, there's nothing left to say on these matters. I'm just rambling now. It's 2AM, and I should get back to cleaning my (now most certainly former) roommate's room.

EDIT: Jesus Christ, what am I even complaining about? Just yesterday, people lost their lives to an act of cruelty. People lost their husbands and wives and brothers and sisters and children. And friends. And family. And here I am, boo-hoo-hooing about my super-difficult First World problems.
